newsitem.title: MACAU: Business groups dominate Macau election result.
newsitem.headline: Business groups dominate Macau election result.

text.p: Pro-business groups dominated the result of Macau's last legislative election before Portugal ends almost five centuries of colonial rule and returns its last Asian possession to China in 1999.
Six electoral groups representing the interests of business, labour and neighbourhood committees won the eight seats up for grabs in Sunday's poll, according to results issued on Monday.

The Macau Economic Promotion Association, formed by business people, and a group formed by neighbourhood committees each won two seats in the contest for eight directly contested seats in the 23-member Legislative Assembly.

The Macau Prosperity League, the Macau Construction League and the Democratic New Macau, as well as a pro-China labour group, each took one seat each. Voter turnout reached 64 percent, the highest in Macau's history.
Macau's elections are only partly democratic. There are no "political parties", but only electoral interest groups.
In addition to the eight directly elected seats, eight seats were filled by indirect election by functional constituencies in a non-contest -- the number of candidates matched the number of seats.
The remaining seven seats are to be appointed later by Macau's colonial governor, General Vasco Rocha Vieira.
Twelve electoral groups ran in the election, representing interests ranging from labour, neighbourhood associations, business, and liberal political interests.
Macau, a territory of 424,000 people, most of them ethnic Chinese, lies on the southern tip of China along the Pearl River estuary.
